title: Control Board Fault
shortDescription: The main control board has detected an internal error.
fullDescription:
Error F1 on a Wolf cooktop indicates the electronic control board has failed an internal self-diagnostic check. This can be caused by a power surge, moisture ingress, or a component failure on the board.

Most F1 faults require control board replacement. Before replacing, attempt a hard reset by removing power at the breaker for 10 minutes.

causes.cause: Moisture or liquid ingress onto the control

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off power at breaker for 10 minutes, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for moisture
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooktop (qualified only); look for liquid damage on control.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement control module matching model number.

whenToCallPro: Recommended — Wolf cooktop electronics are complex and warranty may be voided by DIY repair.

faq.a: Yes, if the unit is within the 2-year Wolf parts-and-labor warranty.

title: Induction Generator Over-Temperature
fullDescription:
On Wolf induction cooktops, F2 indicates the induction generator (power electronics beneath the cooking surface) has exceeded safe operating temperature. The cooktop suspends heating until it cools.

Check that ventilation beneath the cooktop is unobstructed and that the cooling fan is operational. Cabinet airflow requirements are strict on induction models.

causes.cause: Blocked cooling fan intake or exhaust

fixSteps.title: Allow to cool
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off and wait 30 minutes for generator to cool.

fixSteps.title: Check ventilation
fixSteps.instruction: Clear items from cabinet below cooktop; confirm cutout meets Wolf specs.

fixSteps.title: Test cooling fan
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for fan during operation; replace if silent.

whenToCallPro: If cabinet clearances cannot be addressed or fan requires generator disassembly.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf induction cooktop F2 overheating fix

faq.a: Wolf typically requires 1 inch cabinet clearance around the generator and a ventilated cabinet below.

title: Cookware Not Detected
shortDescription: The induction burner cannot detect ferrous cookware.
fullDescription:
F3 on a Wolf induction cooktop means the selected burner does not detect compatible cookware. Induction only works with ferrous (magnetic) cookware — cast iron, carbon steel, or induction-rated stainless.

Test cookware with a magnet: if a magnet sticks firmly to the bottom, the cookware is induction-compatible. Also check that the pan diameter meets the burner minimum.

causes.cause: Pan base too small for burner

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: Hold magnet to pan bottom — strong attraction means compatible.

fixSteps.title: Check pan size
fixSteps.instruction: Base should cover at least 50% of the burner zone.

fixSteps.title: Test different pan
fixSteps.instruction: If another compatible pan works, cookware is the issue.

whenToCallPro: Only if all compatible pans fail on a specific burner — then coil may be faulty.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf induction cooktop F3 cookware detection

faq.q: Can I use glass or aluminum pans?
faq.a: No — induction requires ferrous metal. Consider interface disks for aluminum pans.

title: Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: A cooking surface temperature sensor is reporting out-of-range values.
fullDescription:
F4 indicates that one of the glass-surface temperature sensors under the induction zone is open, shorted, or reporting invalid values. These sensors protect the ceramic glass from thermal damage.

Sensors are mounted on the underside of the glass and require access from below. Replacement is moderately complex due to the need to support the glass during service.

fixSteps.title: Identify zone
fixSteps.instruction: Note which burner shows F4 — indicates which sensor to service.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cooktop from countertop; access under-glass sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clip out old, install new with thermal paste.

whenToCallPro: Recommended — removing a Wolf cooktop without damaging the glass requires experience.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf cooktop F4 temperature sensor replacement

faq.a: Each induction zone has its own sensor; F4 isolates to the zone displaying the error.

title: Touch Control Fault
shortDescription: A touch key is stuck or the control glass is contaminated.
fullDescription:
F5 indicates the capacitive touch interface has detected a continuously pressed key — often from spilled liquid, food debris, or a cracked glass surface. The cooktop locks out until the condition clears.

Wipe the surface dry and clean thoroughly. If the error persists with a clean surface, the touch module may have failed.

causes.cause: Liquid or food on touch controls

fixSteps.title: Clean surface
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe with dry microfiber then ceramic cooktop cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker 2 minutes to reset touch calibration.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for cracks
fixSteps.instruction: Look for hairline cracks near control area.

whenToCallPro: If glass is cracked, the entire glass top may need replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf cooktop F5 touch control error fix

faq.a: No — it's a safety lockout until the issue is resolved.

title: Line Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Incoming voltage is too high or too low for safe operation.
fullDescription:
F6 indicates supply voltage measured at the terminal block is outside the acceptable window (typically 208-250V for North American 240V models). The cooktop disables heating to protect components.

This often results from loose connections at the terminal block, undersized feeder cable, or utility voltage problems. Verify with a voltmeter under load.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: With breaker off, measure L1-L2 at terminal block when restored.

fixSteps.title: Tighten lugs
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker, torque terminal lugs to spec with insulated screwdriver.

fixSteps.title: Call electrician
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is out of spec, consult an electrician.

whenToCallPro: Always call a licensed electrician for line-voltage issues beyond tightening lugs.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf cooktop F6 voltage error fix

faq.q: What voltage does my cooktop need?
faq.a: North American Wolf cooktops require 208/240V dedicated circuit; check model rating plate.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Loss of communication between touch panel and induction generator.
fullDescription:
F7 means the touch control module and generator cannot exchange data. The cooktop disables all zones until communication is restored.

Inspect the ribbon/harness between the two modules. A reset often clears transient glitches; persistent errors indicate module failure.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Access generator and reseat data harness on both ends.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Replace affected module if reseating does not resolve.

whenToCallPro: Recommended for most homeowners — generator access is involved.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf cooktop F7 communication error fix

faq.a: Wolf cooktops do not typically have user-updatable firmware; service techs have diagnostic tools.

title: Gas Ignition Failure
shortDescription: A sealed gas burner failed to ignite or flame was lost.
fullDescription:
F8 on Wolf gas and dual-fuel cooktops indicates a burner did not ignite within the ignition window or the flame was lost during operation. The spark module stops repeated attempts after a set number of tries.

Check for proper gas supply, clean ignitor electrode, and clean burner cap/head. Debris and spilled food are the top causes.

causes.cause: Gas valve turned off or supply low

fixSteps.title: Clean burner
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cap and head, wash thoroughly, clear port holes with pin.

fixSteps.title: Align cap
fixSteps.instruction: Seat cap flat on head; tabs must engage notches.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ignitor
fixSteps.instruction: Electrode should be dry, ceramic uncracked. Wipe with alcohol.

whenToCallPro: If multiple burners fail or you smell gas, call a pro immediately.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf gas cooktop F8 ignition error fix

faq.q: Why does the clicking continue after ignition?
faq.a: If flame is lost, spark resumes briefly. Prolonged clicking indicates ignition failure.

title: Flame Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The flame rectification sensor is not detecting a flame despite ignition.
fullDescription:
F9 signals that ignition occurred but the flame sensor (flame rod) did not detect flame current. Without flame detection, the gas valve closes for safety.

The flame rod works by rectifying AC current through the ionized flame plasma. A dirty rod, poor ground, or cracked ceramic prevents detection.
symptoms: Flame lights then gas shuts off

fixSteps.title: Clean flame rod
fixSteps.instruction: Gently scuff rod with fine Scotch-Brite; do not sand.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ceramic
fixSteps.instruction: Look for cracks in insulator — replace if cracked.

fixSteps.title: Verify ground
fixSteps.instruction: Check ground wire continuity from module to chassis.

whenToCallPro: If gas smell persists or ignition module appears burnt.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf gas cooktop F9 flame sensor fix

faq.q: Is the flame rod the same as the ignitor?
faq.a: No — the ignitor sparks; the flame rod senses the flame afterward.

title: Runaway Heating Detected
shortDescription: The cooktop detected heating with no user input and disabled itself.
fullDescription:
F10 is a safety lockout triggered when the controller senses power being delivered to a burner/coil without a corresponding user command. This protects against shorted relays or driver FETs.

The cooktop must not be used until the fault is diagnosed and corrected. Typically this means a shorted relay on the generator or a short in a burner coil.

fixSteps.title: Replace generator or coil
fixSteps.instruction: Tech identifies shorted component and replaces.

whenToCallPro: Always — runaway heating is a serious safety fault.
videoSearchQuery: Wolf cooktop F10 runaway error fix

faq.q: Is it safe to use until service?
faq.a: No. Keep the breaker off until repair is complete.
